title: Coconut and lime coconut-wax jar candle
subtitle: A bright, tropical jar candle with a creamy coconut wax base
excerpt: A coconut-lime jar candle poured in a coconut wax and soy wax blend, fragranced with coconut and lime fragrance oils at 8% of wax weight. Coconut wax gives a naturally white, smooth surface and a clean, even burn. Set and cure at room temperature for one week before the first burn.
sourceNotes: Coconut wax blending ratios: International Group Inc. coconut wax technical data sheet (2022). Coconut wax is soft and benefits from a 10 to 15% soy wax addition to improve adhesion and reduce cracking. Pour temperature for coconut-soy blend: 55 to 60°C. Fragrance load 8% is within the typical flash-point range for coconut and lime fragrance oils (>60°C for both).

recipe.batchNotes: Pour as many jars as needed from a single melt. Keep the fragrance load consistent at 8% of total wax weight.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Cure for one week before the first burn. Coconut wax develops a frosted, chalky surface bloom after pouring, normal and characteristic; it disappears on the first burn.
recipe.temperatureNote: Pour at 55 to 60°C for the cleanest surface. Coconut wax can develop surface cracking if poured too hot or cooled too quickly.
recipe.shelfLifeNotes: Two years in a cool, dry cupboard out of direct sunlight. Fragrance intensity fades after about 18 months. Discard if the wax discolours, the wick tips go black while unused, or the fragrance smells off.

glossaryTerms.definition: The first burn of a new jar candle, which sets the melt pool. Burning until the entire top surface has liquefied prevents the candle from tunnelling down the centre on subsequent burns.

The resting period after pouring, during which the fragrance oil binds fully with the wax. Coconut-wax candles improve with one week of cure; the throw is stronger and the surface bloom (white frosting) settles.
The temperature at which a fragrance or essential oil can ignite if exposed to a flame. Always add fragrance oils to wax that has cooled well below the flash point of the oil.

content.text: Warm the jar gently (a few minutes in a low oven or warm water bath) so the wax adheres on contact. Centre the wick tab in the base of the jar and press down firmly. Thread the wick through the centring bar and rest the bar across the rim to keep the wick straight during the pour.

Melt the coconut wax and soy wax together in the candle-pouring pitcher over a water bath or on the lowest hob setting. Heat to 70°C to melt fully, then let the wax cool to 60°C before adding the fragrance.

When the wax is at 60°C, stir in the fragrance oil thoroughly for 30 seconds. Check the wax is still at or above 55°C, then pour steadily into the prepared jar. Pour in one continuous pour, leaving about 1 cm of wick above the wax surface. Do not move the jar until the wax has fully set.

Leave undisturbed at room temperature for 24 hours, then remove the centring bar and trim the wick to 6 mm. Cure for one week before lighting. Coconut wax may develop a white, chalky surface bloom after pouring, this is the wax's natural texture and disappears on the first burn.
